items.q: How long does the process take?
items.a: Every project is unique and has its own complexity. That said, we usually reach a working prototype within a few weeks. Either way, we set clear expectations right at the start of the project.

items.q: What will I get at the end?
items.a: At the end of the specification process, our clients get an interactive prototype they can click and feel, a strategic specification document, design files, and clear guidelines that let you continue on your own (or continue the project with us).

items.q: I've already been through a specification process. What's special about yours?
items.a: Our whole process is built on certainty for our clients. We want you to see the product's user experience before you commit to development (the long, expensive part). Instead of a PDF that gets shelved or a Figma link, you get a working prototype you can click through to understand the product's user experience.

items.q: What's the difference between a prototype and a finished product?
items.a: A prototype is an interactive model that simulates the user experience. It isn't final code and it comes without the exact design. But it lets you feel, test and refine your product before you invest in development.

items.q: Can I take just part of the process?
items.a: Yes. You can bring us in for every stage of the spiral, or just some of them.

items.q: Do you work with our team?
items.a: Yes. We work alongside development, marketing and SEO teams, and make sure everyone speaks the same brand language.

items.q: How much does it cost to work together?
items.a: Every project is priced by size and complexity. We'd be happy to talk, understand what you're building, and tailor an exact proposal from there.

items.q: What happens after I get the prototype?
items.a: You move on to development with all the files and reports. You don't depend on us, but we're here if you need support in the design and development stages too.
